records.claim: The mispredict recovery algorithm triggers on a branch misprediction flush.
records.quote: By leveraging these extra values after the flush, our scheme can correct subsequent mispredictions starting with the second one.
records.why: Confirms that the predictor leverages register values following a misprediction flush.

records.claim: Instructions finished before the flush retain their digests to supply fresh register values to subsequent branches.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: Directly states that instructions finished before branch resolution enlarge visible values when restarting after a flush.

records.claim: On a misprediction flush, entries with valid == 0 whose payload matches a flushed ROB index are cleared to valid=0 and payload=0.
records.quote: Integrating the path for sending register digests from the execution unit to the predictor and recovering the Tomasulo-like table may present some challenges; we plan to address these in future work.
records.why: The paper explicitly notes that recovering the Tomasulo-like table is left for future work and does not specify how flushed in-flight entries are recovered.
records.open_question: How should the register status table handle flushed in-flight instructions upon a branch misprediction?

records.claim: Instruction decode handling triggers at decode when an instruction writing destination register rd is decoded.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: Confirms that this logic triggers at decode for an instruction writing a destination register.

records.claim: Decoding an instruction writing a destination register invalidates any previous digest for that register.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: Clearing the valid bit at decode invalidates the previous digest because a new definition is in flight.

records.claim: On instruction decode, decay counters for valid digests increment and stale digests are invalidated after 256 decoded instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The paper requires invalidating digests after 256 decoded instructions, but the pseudocode completely omitted decay counter tracking and threshold invalidation.
